  • Text of IGPalermo but corrected against photograph; note that Kaibel followed Alessi's apograph, which does not observe the original layout. ;
  • line.3: ἔτη εἴ[κ]οσι πέν(τε) IMusPalermo 8; ἔτη ε CIG IV 9484; ἔτη ε [μῆνας] IG IV 548
  • line.5: Alessi: ΠΡΟΤΑ; Kirchoff: προτ[έρ]ᾳ; Manni Piraino: πρὸ ⟨ι⟩α’; the two numerals ι α are clearly distinguished by interpuncts and a line above, which joins the top of the iota (whence misinterpretation as Τ).

English translation

Marta Fogagnolo

Here lies Rhodine. She lived for 25 years and died on the eleventh day before the Ides of November.

commentary

This Christian inscription is marked by three Christograms at the beginning and one at the end. Kirchhoff’s and Kaibel’s transcription is inaccurate with regard to the division of the text into lines and was probably based on Alessi’s apographs. The reading of the sequence πρὸ ∙ τ ∙ α in l. 5 is explained by Manni Piraino (1973, 29–30) as a cutter’s error for πρὸ ∙ ∙ α. The interpretation as “the eleventh day before the Ides of November” is preferable to πρὸ γ νωνῶν, since, in this period, dating by the Ides is preferred to dating by the Nones (see IG XIV 524, likewise from Catania). The name of the deceased, Ῥοδίνη, is otherwise unattested in Sicily, although it occurs in Latin inscriptions from Magna Graecia (CIL X 2155, X 2407, both from Puteoli).
